## Why

dnsman already owns DNS records (`services/dns.py` — upsert/delete/propagation,
allowlisted record types, permission-gated REST) and certificates (`Certificate`
with KMS-held keys, ACME DNS-01 issuance and renewal). The admin UI for both
shipped in **#394**.

The missing third piece is the nginx vhost — the thing that actually *serves* the
domain the DNS points at, using the certificate that was just issued. Today it is
a file somebody hand-writes and copies to every node.

Adding it closes the loop: onboarding a domain becomes one screen — add domain,
point A records, request certificate, define vhost — instead of one portal
operation plus three manual steps repeated per node.

## THE constraint: no free-text nginx

**A vhost must never be a text field an admin types nginx directives into.**

An nginx `server` block is a program, not a setting. Anyone who can write one can
`proxy_pass` to the instance metadata service, `root /opt/api/var;` and serve
`django.conf` over HTTP, claim a `server_name` that shadows the API, or weaken
the TLS configuration. A free-text field would move privilege escalation from
"who can write the filesystem" to "who has a portal permission" — and portal
permissions are usually *broader* than box access, not narrower.

So: a **structured model that generates config from a template we control**. The
admin picks from choices; they never write nginx syntax.

```
Vhost
  domain        FK -> dnsman Domain
  kind          static | spa | proxy          (choices)
  root_slug     slug -> renders as /opt/www/<slug>/current
  upstream      FK/choice from declared upstreams, NEVER a free-form URL
  certificate   FK -> dnsman Certificate
  headers       structured, allowlisted keys and values
  is_enabled    bool
```

You cannot proxy to the metadata service if `upstream` is a foreign key.

## Node-side installer: certs and vhosts together

`asyncjobs.certificate_updated` already broadcasts to every runner, but
*"dnsman itself has nothing to install, so the framework handler only logs."*
Build that consumer, and have it handle **both** payloads in one operation:

```
pull desired state (every enabled vhost + its certificate for this deployment)
render into a staging directory
nginx -t the COMPLETE configuration
  pass -> swap in, reload nginx
  fail -> keep the previous generation, raise an incident event
```

**The database is what makes this safe.** One query is a consistent snapshot, so
a vhost can never land referencing a certificate that has not arrived — the
ordering problem that forces manifests and `current` pointers in an S3 design
simply does not exist here.

Two hard requirements:

- **All-or-nothing.** nginx loads the whole configuration or none of it, so one
  bad vhost breaks *every* site on that node. Always validate the complete
  generated set, never an individual file.
- **Keep the last known-good.** A failed generation must leave the node serving
  what it was already serving, and must be visible as an incident. Also keep the
  last rendered generation on disk so a node that cannot reach the database at
  boot still comes up serving — stale config serves, missing config does not.

## Baseline tests — the point is preventing bad configs, not just detecting them

The renderer is security-critical. These are requirements, not suggestions.

**Injection / escape (the most important, and the easiest to under-test).**
Every operator-controllable field — domain name, root slug, header keys and
values, any label — must be tested with nginx metacharacters and newlines:
`;`, `}`, `{`, `#`, `\n`, `\r\n`, `$`, quotes. Assert the input is **rejected**,
not merely escaped where possible. The canonical case to pin:

```
domain = 'example.com; } server { listen 443; root /etc; #'
```

must not render two server blocks. Assert the rendered output contains exactly
one `server {` and that `/etc` appears nowhere.

**Path containment.** `root_slug` values of `../../etc`, `/opt/api/var`,
`..%2f..`, and absolute paths must be rejected. Assert every rendered `root`/
`alias` resolves under the configured www base, using path normalisation rather
than string prefix matching.

**Upstream allowlisting.** Assert an arbitrary URL cannot become an upstream —
specifically `http://169.254.169.254/`, a private RFC1918 address, and a unix
socket path outside the declared set.

**Kind isolation.** A `static` vhost must never emit `proxy_pass`. A `proxy`
vhost must never emit a filesystem `root` outside the www base. Assert on the
rendered text.

**server_name collisions.** Two enabled vhosts claiming the same name is
rejected. Specifically assert a tenant vhost cannot claim the API's own hostname,
since that is the shadowing attack.

**TLS floor.** Assert every rendered vhost carries the expected protocol and
cipher settings, and that no field can override or remove them.

**Golden-file rendering.** Render a representative set and diff against checked-in
expected output, so an accidental template change shows up as a reviewable diff
rather than silently altering every deployment's web server.

**Installer behaviour.** With a deliberately broken generation injected: assert
`nginx -t` is called on the complete set, the swap does NOT happen, the previous
generation is still in place afterwards, and an incident event is recorded.

**Real `nginx -t`.** If nginx is available in the test environment, run the
rendered output through it. If not, mark it an opt-in/slow test rather than
skipping the check silently — a renderer that produces text no one ever fed to
nginx is a renderer that will produce invalid config eventually.

## What this retires

- `certbot_sync.py` entirely — replaced, not extended. No gatekeeper, no S3
  certificate bucket, no `PRIMARY_BALANCER_HOST`, no primary/replica direction.
  A node asks "what should I be serving?" and installs the answer.
- The operator-only `vhosts/` S3 prefix and its IAM policy that were the interim
  plan, along with the "who may write which prefix" problem.
- Hand-copied vhost files, and the coupling that made adding a website require an
  API deploy.

Permissions and audit come free: `RestMeta` perms decide who may create a vhost,
`LOG_CHANGES` records who did.

## Notes

- Depends on the delegation work (**#1422**, **#1423**) for tenant BYO domains,
  but not for domains whose DNS we already control.
- Full reasoning and surrounding topology:
  `django-mojo-skeleton/docs/django_developer/multi_node_deployment_plan.md`.
- Worth deciding early whether `headers` is needed at all in v1 — every
  structured field is another renderer input to test, and the base config
  already sets the security headers.

# Plan

Scoped 2026-08-06 alongside **#1435**, which is additive to Phase C and Phase D
below. Read the "Shared spine" section before building either item.

**Build routing**: inline, session model. Phases are separate build sessions.

## Objective

django-mojo owns nginx vhosts as **structured, validated rows** and installs
certificates + vhosts to every node as **one atomic, `nginx -t`-validated
generation** with a keep-last-known-good rollback. No admin ever types nginx
syntax; no node ever holds config a validator did not produce.

## Shared spine with #1435

Both items hang off exactly two shared artifacts. Build them once, here:

1. **One desired-state endpoint** (Phase C) — the single thing a node polls.
   #1435 extends its payload with a `webapps` key; it does **not** add a second
   endpoint.
2. **One node-side installer** (Phase D) — stage → validate → swap → reload,
   keep-last-known-good. #1435 adds a release-staging step inside the same
   generation lifecycle; it does **not** add a second installer.

If these two are not built as a spine, the pair ends up with two convergence
loops that can disagree about what a node should be serving. That is the whole
reason to scope them together.

## Placement — new app `mojo/apps/edge/`

Both workspecs say "dnsman". **Scoping moves this to a new `edge` app**, and
this is the single decision most worth overturning if you disagree:

- dnsman's charter is DNS + certificates, and it is already 8 models, 11 REST
  modules and 19 test files. Vhost/WebApp/WebAppRelease add 4 more models and a
  filesystem writer.
- Phase D is **privileged node-side code** — it writes files nginx reads and
  shells out to reload nginx. dnsman's own docstrings are built on "this system
  never touches a node". Putting a root-adjacent installer inside it inverts
  that.
- #1435's models contain zero DNS.
- The dependency is one-way (`edge` → `dnsman`), so nothing is lost.

Reversing this is mechanical (move files, rename the app label, regenerate
migrations) but is much cheaper before Phase A than after Phase D.

## Phase A — models + validators, no rendering

Files:
- `mojo/apps/edge/{__init__.py,apps.py}`, `models/__init__.py`, `migrations/`
- `mojo/apps/edge/models/upstream.py`
- `mojo/apps/edge/models/vhost.py`
- `mojo/apps/edge/validators.py`
- `mojo/apps/edge/rest/{__init__.py,upstream.py,vhost.py}`
- register in the test project, then `bin/create_testproject`

### `Upstream` — the object that decides where traffic may go

```
Upstream(models.Model, MojoModel)
  created, modified          (per .claude/rules/models.md)
  group        FK account.Group, null=True   # null = house upstream
  name         CharField(64)                 # slug; unique per group
  kind         http | unix                   # choices
  host         CharField(253) null           # kind=http only
  port         IntegerField null             # kind=http only, 1..65535
  socket_path  CharField(255) null           # kind=unix only
  is_enabled   BooleanField(default=True)
```

`RestMeta`: `VIEW_PERMS = ["view_dns", "manage_dns", "security"]`,
`SAVE_PERMS = ["manage_dns", "security"]`, `CAN_CREATE = False` on the
collection route — creation goes through a REST action gated by
`dnsman.rest.gates.require_platform_admin`. **Creating an upstream is a
platform-admin act**, because this row is the allowlist. A tenant admin selects
from upstreams visible to them (their own group's, plus group-less house rows);
they can never mint one.

Hard denies at validation, for *any* caller including a platform admin:
- `169.254.0.0/16` and `fd00::/8`-style link-local/metadata addresses. There is
  no legitimate reverse proxy to IMDS.
- `socket_path` that does not normalise under `EDGE_SOCKET_BASE`
  (`os.path.commonpath` on `realpath`, never `startswith`).
- Any `host` containing a character outside `[a-z0-9.-]` (so no scheme, no path,
  no port smuggling, no newline).

**Deliberate departure from the workspec's test list:** loopback and RFC1918
hosts are *allowed* for platform admins. The real upstream on every node is
`127.0.0.1:<asgi port>`, and internal services legitimately live on private
addresses. The workspec's "a private RFC1918 address must be rejected" is
satisfied structurally instead — a **tenant** cannot create any upstream at all,
so no tenant-supplied value ever becomes one. The test asserts that, not a
blanket RFC1918 ban, which would forbid the primary use case.

### `Vhost`

```
Vhost(models.Model, MojoModel)
  created, modified
  domain       FK dnsman.Domain, related_name="vhosts", on_delete=CASCADE
  label        CharField(63, blank=True, default="")   # "" = apex, "*" = wildcard
  kind         static | spa | proxy
  upstream     FK edge.Upstream null # proxy only
  certificate  FK dnsman.Certificate, on_delete=PROTECT
  pool         CharField(32, default="default", db_index=True)
  is_enabled   BooleanField(default=True, db_index=True)
```

**There is no `root_slug`.** The workspec sketches one and the first draft of
this plan kept it as a validated `CharField`; the challenge pass killed it.
A tenant-writable slug is a **cross-tenant read primitive** the moment #1435
lands: `/opt/www/<slug>/current` becomes another tenant's installed build
output, and tenant A sets `root_slug` to tenant B's slug to serve B's private
bundle — source maps, embedded config, admin JS — from A's own domain. Every
validator in the draft passed it, because containment was the only question
asked and the string had no owner until #1435 gave it one.

**The web root is derived from the row's own identity** — the rendered `root`
names `<generation>/www/<vhost.id>`, a symlink the installer stages inside the
generation (Phase D), backed by `EDGE_WWW_BASE/<vhost.id>/releases/<version>`.
An integer primary key cannot traverse, cannot collide, and cannot name another
tenant's content — so `validate_root_slug` and the whole containment argument
disappear with it. This is the same structural
move `Upstream` makes for `proxy_pass`, applied to the half of the model where
the draft had left free text. #1435's `WebApp` reaches disk through
`WebApp.vhost` (unique FK), not through a matching string.

`pool` (added on the challenge pass — see the Challenge section) is the
per-node dimension. One column now, filtered by the desired-state endpoint;
retrofitting it after Phase D would mean reworking the generation hash, the
installer and the on-disk layout.

**`server_name` is derived, never stored free-text**: `label + "." + domain.name`,
or `domain.name` when `label == ""`. This is the structural fix for the
shadowing attack — you cannot claim a name under a domain you do not own,
because ownership is the `Domain` FK and `Domain` is already tenant-scoped.
It also makes the workspec's canonical injection case unreachable by
construction: `example.com; } server { ...` is not a valid `Domain.name` (that
model already normalises to IDNA/lowercase) and is not a valid `label`.

`headers` is **dropped from v1** (the workspec's own open question). The base
config sets the security headers; every extra structured field is another
renderer input to test for no current requirement. Adding it later is additive.

Constraints (both shapes already ship in this repo — partial unique at
`mojo/apps/dnsman/models/acme_delegation.py:61`, the check at
`mojo/apps/incident/models/maestro_item_link.py:18`):
- `UniqueConstraint(fields=["domain", "label"], condition=Q(is_enabled=True),
  name="edge_vhost_unique_enabled_server_name")` — two *enabled* vhosts cannot
  claim the same name; disabled rows may sit alongside a live one. **This
  constraint, not `nginx -t`, is the collision defence** — see Phase D.
- `CheckConstraint` enforcing the kind pairing: `proxy` requires `upstream`;
  `static`/`spa` forbid it. Enforced in the DB as well as in `clean()` so a
  service-layer write cannot produce a hybrid row the renderer has no branch
  for.

`RestMeta`: `GROUP_FIELD = "domain__group"` (same as `Certificate`),
`VIEW_PERMS = ["view_dns", "manage_dns", "security"]`,
`SAVE_PERMS = ["manage_dns", "security"]`, `LOG_CHANGES = True`,
`NO_SAVE_FIELDS` covering `id/pk/created/domain`.

**House-vhost guard.** A vhost whose `domain.group_id is None` is platform
property. Reuse the exact shape of
`mojo/apps/dnsman/rest/certificate.py::_guard_house_certificate` — including
its ordering rule: run the model permission check **first**, then the platform
guard, so an unauthenticated caller cannot tell a house vhost from a tenant one
by the status code. Copy that comment; it encodes a non-obvious oracle fix.

### `validators.py`

- `validate_label(label)` → `""`, `"*"`, or `^[a-z0-9]([a-z0-9-]{0,61}[a-z0-9])?$`.
  Rejects dots, `;{}#$`, quotes, `\n`, `\r\n` by construction.
- `server_name_for(vhost)` → derived string.
- `validate_not_reserved(server_name)` → refuse any name in the reserved set.
  Reserved set = `django.conf.settings.ALLOWED_HOSTS` (concrete hostnames only)
  ∪ `settings.get("EDGE_RESERVED_SERVER_NAMES", [], kind="list")`. **Fail
  closed:** if `ALLOWED_HOSTS` is empty or `["*"]` *and*
  `EDGE_RESERVED_SERVER_NAMES` is unset, refuse to enable any vhost and log an
  actionable error. A deployment that cannot name its own API hostname cannot
  protect it, and silently allowing every name is the shadowing attack.
- `validate_certificate_covers(vhost)` → the FK'd `Certificate` must belong to
  the same `Domain` **and** its `common_name`/`sans` must cover the derived
  `server_name` (with wildcard matching: `*.x` covers one label under `x`).
  Blocks attaching an unrelated certificate, which would otherwise be a way to
  make a node serve a cert for a name the vhost's owner does not control.

`tests/test_edge/0_validators.py`, `1_models.py`, `2_rest_permissions.py` —
label / reserved-name / socket-path / certificate-coverage matrices, the kind

## Phase B — renderer + golden files

Files: `mojo/apps/edge/services/render.py`, `mojo/apps/edge/nginx/*.tmpl`,
`tests/test_edge/golden/*.conf`.

- **Not Django templates.** Django's autoescaping is HTML-shaped and does
  nothing useful for nginx, and its presence would imply a safety that is not
  there. Use plain `str` builders over already-validated values.
- **Re-assert at the boundary.** Every value substituted into output passes a
  final whitelist check inside the renderer and raises on any character outside
  it — belt and braces, so a future service-layer write that skips `clean()`
  still cannot reach the file.
- **Kind isolation is structural, not conditional.** Three builder functions:
  `_render_static`, `_render_spa`, `_render_proxy`. The literal string
  `proxy_pass` appears only in `_render_proxy`; `root ` appears only in the
  static/spa builders. Assert on rendered text as the workspec requires, but the
  guarantee comes from the code shape.
- **TLS floor** emitted unconditionally from `EDGE_TLS_PROTOCOLS` /
  `EDGE_TLS_CIPHERS` settings. No model field feeds it — there is no field that
  could.
- `render_generation(vhosts)` returns `{filename: text}` plus a **generation
  id** = `sha256` over the canonical (sorted) serialisation of the inputs. That
  id is what makes the installer idempotent.

### Phase B tests
`3_render_injection.py` (the workspec's metacharacter matrix, asserting
*rejection*, plus the canonical `example.com; } server {` case → exactly one
`server {`, no `/etc`), `4_render_golden.py` (checked-in expected output).

## Phase C — desired-state endpoint

File: `mojo/apps/edge/rest/node.py`.

```
GET /api/edge/desired_state?pool=default
{
  "generation": "<sha256>",
  "vhosts": [ {id, server_name, kind, upstream:{kind,host,port,socket_path},
               certificate: <cert id>} ],
  "certificates": [ {id, common_name, not_after} ]     # ids and metadata only
}
```

**Pool-scoped, defaulting to one pool.** The endpoint filters on
`Vhost.pool`, defaulting to `"default"`, and the generation hash is computed
over the filtered set. A single-pool fleet behaves exactly like the
fleet-global design the first draft proposed; the difference is that a staging
pool, an isolated tenant node, or a geo-pinned vhost later costs one filter
clause instead of a rework of Phase B and Phase D. (The first draft argued
per-node scoping would be "a second source of truth"; that argument defeats a
second *endpoint*, not a *column* on the same row — see the Challenge section.)

**Auth — this is the part the first draft got wrong, and it mattered.**

Add `edge_node` to `APIKEY_PERMS_PROTECTION_DEFAULTS` in
`mojo/apps/account/models/api_key.py` mapped to `sys.edge_node`, exactly as
`geoip_sync` and `dnsman_acme_federation` already are.

Gate both node endpoints with
**`@md.requires_global_perms("edge_node", allow_api_keys=True)`** — the same
decorator `mojo/apps/account/rest/device.py:134` uses for the geoip sync
receiver. **Never `@md.requires_perms`.**

`requires_perms` has a group fallback that is ON by default
(`REQUIRES_PERMS_IS_GROUP`, `mojo/decorators/auth.py:12`, used at
`auth.py:160-178`): when the caller's global permission dict misses, it
re-checks against a **client-supplied `?group=` param**. And the `GroupMember`
side of the protection floor is empty by default —
`_member_perms_protection()` (`mojo/apps/account/models/member.py:9-12`)
returns `{}`, so an unlisted perm falls through to
`req_member.has_permission(["manage_group", ...])` (`member.py:100-102`) and any
tenant group admin can grant themselves `edge_node` inside their own group. The
`APIKEY_PERMS_PROTECTION` floor closes the ApiKey path only; it does not touch
this one.

Under `requires_perms` the exploit is three ordinary REST calls: grant yourself
the member permission, call `desired_state?group=<your own group>`, receive
every vhost on the fleet — then call the material endpoint below the same way
and receive **every certificate private key referenced by any enabled vhost,
including every house certificate**. That is strictly worse than the hole
`require_platform_admin` exists to close, introduced as the workaround for it.
`requires_global_perms` authorizes on the caller's global `User.permissions`
(or superuser) only and never consults the member/group fallback.

### Blocker found in scoping — nodes cannot use the existing material endpoint

`GET /api/dnsman/certificate/material/<pk>` is the documented way a serving host
pulls key material. It cannot work for a node key today:
`_guard_house_certificate` → `require_platform_admin`, and that gate
**refuses key-backed sessions outright** (`mojo/apps/dnsman/rest/gates.py:42`).
Every platform vhost sits on a house (group-less) domain, so a node's API key is
refused on exactly the certificates it must install.

**Resolution (do not weaken `require_platform_admin` — that gate is
deliberate):** add a node-facing sibling,
`GET /api/edge/material/<int:pk>`, gated the same way
(`requires_global_perms("edge_node", allow_api_keys=True)`), which serves
material **only** for a certificate referenced by an enabled `Vhost`. That is
strictly tighter than the existing endpoint for this use — a node key can read
what it must install and nothing else — and it leaves the platform gate
untouched. Reuse the existing endpoint's status checks, KMS-unavailable 503
handling and access log line verbatim.

### Phase C tests
`5_desired_state.py` — payload shape and generation stability; pool filtering;
an ordinary `manage_dns` key is refused; an ApiKey cannot self-mint `edge_node`
(the `APIKEY_PERMS_PROTECTION` floor test, mirroring the existing `geoip_sync`
one); **a member-scoped `edge_node` grant plus `?group=<own group>` is refused**
— this is the regression test for the draft's authorization bug and it does not
exist on the ApiKey path; node material is served for a referenced cert and
refused for an unreferenced one.

## Phase D — node-side installer

Files: `mojo/apps/edge/services/installer.py`, `mojo/apps/edge/asyncjobs.py`,
`mojo/apps/edge/cronjobs.py`.

### On-disk layout

```
EDGE_ROOT (default /opt/api/var/edge)
  generations/<generation>/
      nginx.conf                       # harness wrapper, pre-filter nginx -t only
      conf.d/*.conf
      certs/<cert-id>/{fullchain.pem,privkey.pem}    0600, app-user owned
      www/<vhost-id> -> /opt/www/<vhost-id>/releases/<version>   (#1435)
  current -> generations/<generation>
  installed.json                       # {generation, installed_at}
```

**The web-root symlinks live INSIDE the generation** (`www/<vhost-id>`), and a
static/spa vhost's `root` names `<generation>/www/<vhost-id>`. The first draft
put them at `/opt/www/<slug>/current`, outside the generation — which meant a
failed `nginx -t` abandoned the config swap but left the *content* already
moved, so the node served the new bundle under the old config: a state neither
generation describes, and exactly the "two convergence loops that disagree"
failure the shared spine exists to prevent. One `os.replace` of `current` now
swaps config and content together, and rollback reverts both.

`/etc/nginx/conf.d/mojo.conf` is a one-line
`include /opt/api/var/edge/current/conf.d/*.conf;` — written once at provisioning
time, never by this code.

**Rendered configs reference certificates by absolute *generation* path, not
through the `current` symlink.** This is the detail that makes the whole thing
work: `nginx -t -c <staging>/nginx.conf` must validate against the *new*
generation's certs, which it can only do if the staged config names them
directly. The swap is then a single `os.replace` of the `current` symlink plus a
reload, and rollback is repointing `current` at a retained generation whose
config still names its own still-present files. Keep `EDGE_KEEP_GENERATIONS`
(default 5).

### Sequence

```
fetch desired_state
if generation == installed.json.generation: return  (idempotent no-op)
render into generations/<new>/, pull each certificate's material, write 0600
  a certificate whose material cannot be fetched:
      house vhost  -> abort the whole install (see below)
      tenant vhost -> EXCLUDE that vhost from the generation + report_event
stage releases (#1435 Phase I) and the www/<vhost-id> links
nginx -t -c generations/<new>/nginx.conf          # cheap pre-filter
  non-zero -> abort, `current` untouched, incident, raise
os.replace(current -> generations/<new>)          # nothing has reloaded yet
nginx -t                                          # against the REAL /etc/nginx/nginx.conf
  non-zero, or stderr matches "conflicting server name"
           -> os.replace(current -> previous); incident; raise. No reload
              happened, so the running config is untouched.
  zero     -> systemctl reload nginx; write installed.json;
              prune to EDGE_KEEP_GENERATIONS
```

**Why validation happens after the swap, not only before.** A harness
`nginx.conf` only approximates the real one: `map`, `upstream`,
`limit_req_zone` and `proxy_cache_path` blocks defined in the real config and
referenced by generated output pass or fail differently under the harness. The
real test is the real config. This is safe because **nginx serves the running
configuration until something reloads it** — a bad `current` that fails
validation is reverted before any reload, so it is never loaded. The staging
pre-filter is kept anyway: it catches most breakage without touching `current`
at all.

**`nginx -t` does NOT catch server_name collisions.** A duplicate name is a
*warning* — `conflicting server name "x" on 0.0.0.0:443, ignored` — and nginx
still exits 0, silently dropping one of the blocks. Worse, the platform's own
API server block lives in the real config, not in the generated set, so the
shadowing attack is invisible to the harness and non-fatal to nginx. The
defences that actually work are the Phase A enabled-uniqueness constraint and
`validate_not_reserved`; the stderr grep above is a third net, not the first.
Do not let the plan (or the tests) imply `nginx -t` covers this.

**Why a tenant's un-fetchable certificate must not abort the install.** The
material fetch can fail for reasons unrelated to the row — `KSMSecrets` returns
an empty mapping when KMS decryption fails, and the material endpoint answers
503 (`mojo/apps/dnsman/rest/certificate.py:132-134`). With a single abort path,
one tenant's broken certificate freezes convergence for the **entire pool**,
including an urgent renewal of the platform's own API certificate — and it fails
silent-but-serving until something expires. nginx's all-or-nothing loading
requires the *generation* be complete; it does not require the generation to
contain every vhost. So: drop the tenant vhost, report one incident per
exclusion, converge everything else. A house vhost failing is still a hard
abort — that is the platform's own serving path.

**Privilege boundary — name it, do not paper over it.** The installer runs as the
app user in the job runner. Two operations need more: `nginx -t` and
`systemctl reload nginx`. Both are shelled out through a **constant argv list**
in code, never composed from row data, behind a narrow sudoers rule. Writing
that sudoers file and the `mojo.conf` include is **django-mojo-skeleton work**
and is a cross-repo dependency of this phase, not something this item ships.

State plainly in the docs what this changes: the structured-model constraint at
the top of this workspec defends against a malicious *admin*; it does nothing
about a compromised *API process*, which now has a path to nginx config. The
bound on that is the sudoers narrowness plus the app user owning only `EDGE_ROOT`
— not the renderer.

### Triggers
- Broadcast job `edge.install_generation` on channel `edge`. Add `edge` to
  `DEFAULT_CHANNELS` in `mojo/apps/jobs/__init__.py` **and** document it for
  `JOBS_ALLOWED_CHANNELS`. (Correction to the first draft: `publish` does *not*
  refuse undeclared channels by default — `JOBS_ALLOWED_CHANNELS` is `None`
  out of the box, which is monitor mode: the publish routes anyway and files a
  `jobs:undeclared_channel` incident, `mojo/apps/jobs/__init__.py:40-50`. The
  remedy is the same; a deployment that has turned enforcement on and only
  updates one of the two lists gets an incident storm.)
- `mojo/apps/dnsman/asyncjobs.py::certificate_updated` grows one line: enqueue
  an edge install. Its existing log line stays.
- A cron sweep (`EDGE_CONVERGE_MINUTES`, default 10) so a node that missed a
  broadcast, booted from an AMI, or had its runner stopped converges on its own.

### Stale-serves-on-boot
No code path deletes or repoints `current` on a failed pull. A node whose DB is
unreachable at boot starts nginx from the retained generation. This is an
absence-of-behaviour property, so it gets an explicit test rather than a comment.

### Phase D tests
`6_installer.py` — deliberately broken generation: `nginx -t` invoked on the
complete set, **`current` ends up back at the previous generation and no reload
was issued**, incident recorded, job raises; a `conflicting server name` warning
on stderr with exit 0 is treated as failure; a tenant certificate that cannot be
fetched is excluded and the rest converge, while a house one aborts; idempotent
no-op on an unchanged generation; retention prune; rollback by repointing; a
failed fetch leaves `current` alone.
`7_nginx_real.py` — `@th.requires_extra("extended")`, runs the golden output
through a real `nginx -t`. **Fails, does not skip,** when the tag is selected and
nginx is absent — a silent skip is how a renderer nobody validated ships.

## Phase E — retire `certbot_sync.py`

Cross-repo (django-mojo-skeleton): delete the script, the S3 cert prefix, the
`vhosts/` prefix and its IAM policy, and `PRIMARY_BALANCER_HOST`. **Not shipped
by this item** — django-mojo's side is the docs note in
`docs/django_developer/edge/` recording the replacement and the migration order
(install Phase D on every node → verify `installed.json` fleet-wide → then
remove the old path).

## Testing

Baseline before the first edit of each phase:
`bin/run_tests --agent -t test_edge -t test_dnsman -t test_jobs -t test_account`.
Phase A and Phase C touch models/migrations and
`mojo/apps/account/models/api_key.py`, which are `build-baseline.md` escalation
triggers → **whole suite** for those two phases. Read
`testproject/var/test_failures.json`, never terminal output. Run
`bin/create_testproject` after the Phase A models land.

## Documentation

- `docs/django_developer/edge/README.md` — the model shape, the generation
  lifecycle, the privilege boundary, the settings (`EDGE_ROOT`, `EDGE_WWW_BASE`,
  `EDGE_SOCKET_BASE`, `EDGE_RESERVED_SERVER_NAMES`, `EDGE_TLS_*`,
  `EDGE_KEEP_GENERATIONS`, `EDGE_CONVERGE_MINUTES`), and the skeleton-side
  provisioning it depends on.
- `docs/web_developer/` — the Vhost/Upstream REST surface, permissions required,
  and the `edge_node` machine endpoints.
- Index both in the respective `README.md`.

## Suggested decomposition

Five phases, each its own build session and commit. If you want them tracked
separately, they should be **sub-items of #1433** (board convention: one level of
nesting, same board) — not filed yet, ask first.

| Phase | Rough size |
|---|---|
| A models + validators + REST | 1 commit, ~3 test files |
| B renderer + golden | 1 commit, 2 test files |
| C desired-state + node material + `edge_node` floor | 1 commit, 1 test file |
| D installer + triggers | 1 commit, 2 test files |
| E docs + retirement note | 1 commit |

**One dependency must be filed separately, in django-mojo-skeleton**: the
sudoers rule for `nginx -t` / `systemctl reload nginx` and the
`/etc/nginx/conf.d/mojo.conf` include. It blocks *verification* of Phase D, and
therefore Phase E and all of #1435's node-side value. Phase D can be written and
unit-tested without it; it cannot be proven on a node. Not filed yet — ask
first.

### Challenge

One fresh-context agent red-teamed the draft of this plan and #1435's together.
Every objection below was re-verified against source by the scoping session
before disposition. This was not a light pass — two of the findings were
security defects in the draft.

**1. `@md.requires_perms("edge_node")` was wrong, and would have shipped a
fleet-wide private-key disclosure. — `amended`.**
The draft called it "global, not group-scoped". It is not: `requires_perms`
falls back to a client-supplied `?group=` (`mojo/decorators/auth.py:12`,
`:160-178`), and unlike the ApiKey floor the `GroupMember` protection map is
empty by default (`mojo/apps/account/models/member.py:9-12`, `:100-102`), so any
tenant group admin can grant themselves the perm in their own group and read the
whole fleet's serving config *and* every referenced certificate's private key.
Verified in source. Phase C now specifies
`requires_global_perms("edge_node", allow_api_keys=True)` — the decorator whose
docstring (`auth.py:245-271`) describes precisely this escalation — plus a
regression test for the member-grant path, which no existing test covers.

**2. `Vhost.root_slug` was a cross-tenant read primitive once #1435 lands. —
`amended`.** Tenant A points `root_slug` at tenant B's `WebApp.slug` and serves
B's private build output from A's domain. Containment validation passes; it was
the only question the draft asked, because the string had no owner until #1435
gave it one. Found only because the items were scoped as a pair.
Fixed more aggressively than the challenger proposed: they suggested an
ownership-validated `WebApp` FK; the plan instead **deletes the field** and
derives the root from `vhost.id`. An integer cannot traverse, collide, or name
another tenant's content, the containment validator disappears, and Phase A
gains no dependency on #1435's models.

**3. The web-root symlink sat outside the atomic generation. — `amended`.**
Keep-last-known-good held for config and not for content. Phase D now nests
`www/<vhost-id>` inside the generation directory so one `os.replace` swaps both.

**4. `nginx -t` against a harness config does not validate what the draft
claimed. — `amended`.** Two distinct gaps, both real: a duplicate `server_name`
is a warning and exits 0 (so the shadowing attack *passes* validation), and
harness-vs-real config divergence over `map`/`upstream`/`limit_req_zone` cuts
both ways. Phase D now swaps first and validates against the real config before
any reload — safe because nginx serves the running config until reloaded — greps
stderr for `conflicting server name`, and states plainly that the DB constraint
and reserved-name check are the collision defence.

**5. One tenant's un-fetchable certificate froze fleet-wide convergence. —
`amended`.** Phase D now excludes un-installable tenant vhosts with a
per-exclusion incident and hard-fails only on house vhosts.

**6. Fleet-global scoping was the weakest resolved decision. — `amended`.**
The challenger's rebuttal is correct and the draft's reasoning was sloppy: "a
second source of truth" is an argument against a second *endpoint*, not against
a *column*. `Vhost.pool` costs one column and one filter clause now; adding the
dimension after Phase D would mean reworking the generation hash, the installer
and the on-disk layout.

**7. "`publish` refuses undeclared channels" was false. — `amended`.** Default
is monitor mode (`mojo/apps/jobs/__init__.py:40-50`). Remedy unchanged,
justification corrected.

**8. The new `edge` app was challenged and found sound. — `rebutted`, by the
challenger itself.** It went looking for a weak call here (the draft flagged it
as the most overturnable) and concluded the four reasons each verify, that the
requester wrote "dnsman" as a locator rather than an architecture decision, and
that it would ship `edge`. Recorded because a pre-flagged decision surviving an
adversarial read is worth more than the flag.

**9. Scope realism: the decomposition is honest, the item count is not. —
`amended`.** Nine phases, three whole-suite baselines, two cross-repo
dependencies. Phase D in particular cannot be *verified* in this repo at all —
its acceptance criterion (sudoers + the `/etc/nginx/conf.d/mojo.conf` include)
lives in django-mojo-skeleton. That is now stated as a blocking dependency to
file, not a row in a size table.

**Also checked and found sound**, with no change required:
`require_platform_admin` really does refuse key-backed sessions
(`gates.py:42-46`) and really does block a node key from house certificate
material — the blocker Phase C works around is genuine;
`APIKEY_PERMS_PROTECTION_DEFAULTS` really does hold its floor on the ApiKey
path; `ApiKey.rotate_token()` behaves exactly as #1435's D3 assumes;
`mojo/helpers/aws/` genuinely has no STS and `generate_presigned_url` is
`get_object`-only; the partial `UniqueConstraint` and the kind-pairing
`CheckConstraint` are both expressible and both already shipped elsewhere in
this repo; dropping `headers` from v1 and defaulting `auto_promote` to False
drew no objection.
